title: Satellite plays iconic game in world’s 1st demonstration of orbital voice control

ai.summary: A satellite in space played the Doom video game after receiving a voice command from a rooftop in Oslo, Norway, marking a historic demonstration of orbital voice control. The experiment, conducted by radio amateurs with the European Space Agency, used open-source tools to transmit and interpret the command successfully.

facts.claim: A satellite in space played the Doom video game after receiving a voice command from a rooftop in Oslo, Norway
facts.quote: A satellite went knee-deep in the dead, after a voice command from the ground activated the Doom video game in space.

facts.claim: The experiment, conducted by radio amateurs with the European Space Agency
facts.quote: OPS-SAT Space Lab managed the experiment on behalf of ESA.

facts.claim: The satellite played Doom after receiving the command
facts.quote: The historic voice command on July 27— in part, “PRETTY play Doom Doom Doom”— came from a rooftop in Oslo, and was spoken at night by Jon Bergli Heier (LB9BJ). PRETTY picked up the transmission, transcribed the command using on-board voice recognition, and then — just like a typical evening gamer—opened up Doom for a play session.
But the transmission clearly worked, powered by open-source tools including GNU Radio (which handled the signal processing) and Sherpa-ONNX (speech recognition).
